diplomacyR

diplomacyR is a complete engine for the board game Diplomacy on the standard seven-power pre-1914 map. It gives you a rules-accurate adjudicator for simultaneous movement, the full phase machine from Spring 1901 to a solo victory, scriptable bots, batch simulation with outcome analysis, and a shiny application for interactive play.

Diplomacy has no dice. Every player writes orders for every unit in secret, all the orders are revealed at once, and one set of rules decides what actually happened — including the cases where the outcome of one order depends on the outcome of another that depends back on the first. Getting that right is what most of this package is.

Installation 

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("r-heller/diplomacyR")

A first turn 

library(diplomacyR)

game <- dp_new_game()
game
#> <dp_game> Spring 1901 (movement phase)
#> Russia    4 centres   4 units
#> Austria   3 centres   3 units
#> England   3 centres   3 units
#> France    3 centres   3 units
#> Germany   3 centres   3 units
#> Italy     3 centres   3 units
#> Turkey    3 centres   3 units

Orders are written the way players write them, and resolved with dp_adjudicate(). Here France attacks Burgundy with support while Germany attacks it alone: two against one.

result <- dp_adjudicate(game, dp_parse_orders(c(
  "France: A Par - Bur",
  "France: A Mar S A Par - Bur",
  "Germany: A Mun - Bur"
)))

result$orders[result$orders$loc %in% c("par", "mar", "mun"), ]
#> <dp_orders> (3 orders)
#> ✓ France: A Mar S A Par - Bur
#> ✓ France: A Par - Bur
#> ✗ Germany: A Mun - Bur

Every power that was not ordered simply held, which is what the rules say happens to a unit with no orders. dp_advance() applies the result and steps the season, phase and year.

game <- dp_advance(game, result)
game
#> <dp_game> Fall 1901 (movement phase)
#> Russia    4 centres   4 units
#> Austria   3 centres   3 units
#> England   3 centres   3 units
#> France    3 centres   3 units
#> Germany   3 centres   3 units
#> Italy     3 centres   3 units
#> Turkey    3 centres   3 units

To watch a whole game instead, hand it to the bots:

history <- dp_play(bots = "greedy", max_years = 3, seed = 1)
dp_power_summary(history)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 6
#>   power   turns start_centres final_centres peak_centres mean_centres
#>   <chr>   <int>         <int>         <int>        <int>        <dbl>
#> 1 Germany    11             3             8            8         5.27
#> 2 Turkey     11             3             7            7         5.18
#> 3 France     11             3             4            4         3.82
#> 4 Italy      11             3             4            4         3.09
#> 5 Austria    11             3             3            3         3   
#> 6 England    11             3             3            3         3   
#> 7 Russia     11             4             2            4         3.09

What is in the box

  • The board. dp_map() loads the standard 75-province, 34-centre map with separate army and fleet adjacency graphs and per-coast fleet locations.
  • The adjudicator. dp_adjudicate() resolves movement phases — supports, support cutting, standoffs, dislodgement, head-to-head battles, convoys and convoy paradoxes. dp_retreat() and dp_build() handle the other two phase types, and dp_advance() drives the season machine.
  • Orders. dp_parse_orders() reads standard notation in all its usual spellings; format() renders any order set back to canonical text; dp_legal_orders() enumerates everything the rules currently permit.
  • Bots. Four of them — "random", "hold", "greedy" and the experimental "negotiator" — through dp_ai_orders(), plus dp_step() and dp_play() to drive whole games.
  • Simulation and analysis. dp_simulate() runs batches, dp_stats() and dp_power_summary() summarise them, and the dp_plot_*() functions return ggplot2 objects for the board, supply-centre trajectories, win rates and where the fighting happens.

Rules conformance

The adjudicator is validated against the Diplomacy Adjudicator Test Cases, the reference suite assembled by Lucas B. Kruijswijk. It passes all 130 movement-phase cases, sections 6.A to 6.G: legality and coasts, circular movement, supports and dislodges, head-to-head battles, convoys, convoy paradoxes and convoying to one’s own area. Where the suite allows more than one defensible answer, the engine implements the option it marks as preferred. The encoded cases ship with the package under extdata/datc.

The application 

dp_run_app()

A shiny interface with an interactive board, an order editor that checks legality as you type, a turn adjudicator, a replayable history, analysis charts and a batch-simulation runner. It needs shiny, bslib and DT, which are suggested rather than required.
